title: Server config file + token-accurate usage

title: Unify model cache on the Hugging Face hub cache

title: Multi-model server: honor request model, warm pool, hot-swap, LRU

title: bound the loaded-model registry: safe max_loaded default + expose it to placement/restart
description:
## Context

vqtrs-api is dpty-managed on genaihulk and reached **91.4 GB** of anonymous heap in ~9 h (2026-10-02 JetsamEvent-2026-10-02-115935/120135.ips), tripping Jetsam twice next to sushi's 71.7 GB LLM and 2x ~17 GB VM stacks. Correction to the earlier "growing index" premise: **vqtrs is stateless per request** — the API handlers and fastembed/Qwen3 backends are all per-call, and vqtrs never stores embeddings or builds an in-memory index. The unbounded vector is the **model Registry** (`crates/vqtrs-api/src/registry.rs`): an LRU cache that, at `max_loaded = 0`, **never evicts**.

## Gap

- `ServerConfig.max_loaded` **defaults to `0` = unbounded** (`crates/vqtrs-api/src/config.rs`). With no config file, vqtrs runs fully default and keeps every distinct model the workload touches resident forever (Qwen3-0.6B/4B/8B on the CPU-F32 candle path plus the ONNX catalog).
- The bound is only settable via a config file; there is **no CLI/env flag** for `max_loaded` (it's config-file-only in `main.rs`), so a dpty recipe cannot express it inline without a config file.
- No enforcement: LRU only evicts on *count* exceeding `max`, keyed by distinct model name. A workload that touches many model ids (or a single heavy Qwen3-8B) still blows the envelope in resident bytes.

## Requested

1. Change the **default** `max_loaded` from `0` to a bounded, safe value so an unconfigured server cannot accumulate unbounded resident models.
2. Add a **CLI flag / env var** (e.g. `--max-loaded` / `VQTRS_MAX_LOADED`) parallel to the existing `--model`/`--port`, so the dpty recipe can express the bound inline without relying on an on-disk config file.
3. Optionally consider a **resident-bytes ceiling** (not just a model-count ceiling), or document that `max_loaded` caps count only and heavy models (Qwen3-8B on CPU F32) can still be large.

## Positive-outcome proof

- `vqtrs-api --help` (or `--print-schema`) shows a `max_loaded`/`--max-loaded` knob with a non-zero default.
- A server started with **no** config file and `max_loaded` left at default no longer keeps N distinct models resident beyond the bound; make requests for many models and show resident footprint stays bounded (e.g. RSS plateaus under the bound, or LRU-evicts to keep count <= max).

## Notes

- Immediate mitigation already applied on the box: `~/Library/Application Support/vqtrs/config.toml` sets `max_loaded = 8`, pinned via `--config` in the dpty recipe (`vqtrs/vqtrs-api` rev 2). This issue tracks the durable in-repo fix.
- Placement-side ceiling is tracked separately as `dpty-p64x` (byteowlz/dpty).

title: vqtrs-api stops answering all requests after concurrent or large embedding batches
description:
Observed on GenAIHulk (macOS arm64, M2 Ultra), 2026-10-04, vqtrs-api run by dpty (recipe vqtrs/vqtrs-api), port 3010, model Qdrant/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx, config max_loaded = 8.

Symptoms
- After the trigger, even a 1-text POST /v1/embeddings gets no response (curl -m 8/15/30 -> http 000, timeout) on every attempt.
- The vqtrs-api process stays alive at ~0-0.1% CPU, macOS process state "U" (uninterruptible wait) or "R" without progress. It is not busy computing.
- dpty still reports the instance as Running, so nothing restarts it. Recovery: `dpty stop --recipe vqtrs/vqtrs-api` (dpty respawns a new instance, healthy after ~40 s).

Triggers seen (three wedges in about an hour)
1. 8 concurrent clients, each POSTing 32-text batches (16 batches total, ThreadPoolExecutor(8)): the client side timed out and the server stopped responding to everything.
2. A single 512-text request issued shortly after a successful 512-text request (which took 4.1 s).
3. A real workload: Python client (urllib, 30 s timeout, one retry) sending sequential 256-text batches of mixed code/prose chunks (<= 800 chars each). It failed on its first batch, and the server was wedged afterwards.
Stable afterwards: sequential 128-text batches, 20+ consecutive requests, including real code-heavy chunks, at ~230-370 texts/s.

What the code already does (so these are NOT the cause)
- crates/vqtrs-api/src/main.rs `embeddings` runs inference inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so the async executor is not blocked by inference.
- crates/vqtrs-core/src/embed.rs guards the ONNX TextEmbedding with a Mutex, so concurrent requests serialize on it. That alone should queue, not deadlock.

Hypotheses to test (ranked, each falsifiable)
1. Memory pressure: large batches or many queued requests grow RSS (the config comment records earlier JetsamEvent incidents at 91-97 GB). State "U" on macOS commonly means waiting on page-in. Check: record RSS / memory pressure while reproducing; if RSS jumps before the wedge, this is it.
2. ONNX Runtime intra-op thread pool deadlock when sessions are driven from several blocking threads, or by very large batches. Check: reproduce with ORT intra-op threads set to 1; if the wedge disappears, this is it.
3. Unbounded backlog: clients that time out and retry leave their original requests holding blocking-pool threads queued on the engine mutex, so work accumulates without limit. Check: count in-flight blocking tasks during the repro.
4. Registry lock (crates/vqtrs-api/src/registry.rs get_or_load) held across a slow load or an eviction (max_loaded = 8) while other requests wait. Check: log lock acquire/release around get_or_load during the repro.

Expected behavior / acceptance
- The server never stops serving: under overload it rejects or queues with a bound (e.g. 429/503 with Retry-After, or 413 for oversized batches), and keeps answering other requests (including a /health endpoint if one exists).
- Add a cap on in-flight embedding work (semaphore) and on batch size (configurable; reject above it instead of attempting it).
- If a wedge can still happen, it must be detectable: a health endpoint that dpty can probe, so dpty restarts the instance instead of reporting Running.

Proof of fix (required)
- A load-test script in the repo (e.g. scripts/ or an ignored integration test) that reproduces triggers 1 and 2 against a locally started vqtrs-api: 8 concurrent clients x 32 texts, and back-to-back 512-text requests, for >= 2 minutes.
- Pass criterion: throughout and after the run, a 1-text probe request answers within 2 s every time; overload produces 429/503/413 responses instead of hangs; RSS stays bounded.
- Show the script failing (wedging) on the current main and passing after the fix.

Context: found while building a Kompressor training dataset (MiniLM retrieval embeddings, ~44k texts). The client side now uses 128-text sequential batches with timeouts and a resumable cache as a workaround. vqtrs is shared by other local tools, which would hang the same way.

title: vqtrs-api stops answering all requests after concurrent or large embedding batches
description:
Observed on GenAIHulk (macOS arm64, M2 Ultra), 2026-10-04, vqtrs-api run by dpty (recipe vqtrs/vqtrs-api), port 3010, model Qdrant/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-onnx, config max_loaded = 8.

Symptoms
- After the trigger, even a 1-text POST /v1/embeddings gets no response (curl -m 8/15/30 -> http 000, timeout) on every attempt.
- The vqtrs-api process stays alive at ~0-0.1% CPU, macOS process state "U" (uninterruptible wait) or "R" without progress. It is not busy computing.
- dpty still reports the instance as Running, so nothing restarts it. Recovery: `dpty stop --recipe vqtrs/vqtrs-api` (dpty respawns a new instance, healthy after ~40 s).

Triggers seen (three wedges in about an hour)
1. 8 concurrent clients, each POSTing 32-text batches (16 batches total, ThreadPoolExecutor(8)): the client side timed out and the server stopped responding to everything.
2. A single 512-text request issued shortly after a successful 512-text request (which took 4.1 s).
3. A real workload: Python client (urllib, 30 s timeout, one retry) sending sequential 256-text batches of mixed code/prose chunks (<= 800 chars each). It failed on its first batch, and the server was wedged afterwards.
Stable afterwards: sequential 128-text batches, 20+ consecutive requests, including real code-heavy chunks, at ~230-370 texts/s.

What the code already does (so these are NOT the cause)
- crates/vqtrs-api/src/main.rs `embeddings` runs inference inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, so the async executor is not blocked by inference.
- crates/vqtrs-core/src/embed.rs guards the ONNX TextEmbedding with a Mutex, so concurrent requests serialize on it. That alone should queue, not deadlock.

Hypotheses to test (ranked, each falsifiable)
1. Memory pressure: large batches or many queued requests grow RSS (the config comment records earlier JetsamEvent incidents at 91-97 GB). State "U" on macOS commonly means waiting on page-in. Check: record RSS / memory pressure while reproducing; if RSS jumps before the wedge, this is it.
2. ONNX Runtime intra-op thread pool deadlock when sessions are driven from several blocking threads, or by very large batches. Check: reproduce with ORT intra-op threads set to 1; if the wedge disappears, this is it.
3. Unbounded backlog: clients that time out and retry leave their original requests holding blocking-pool threads queued on the engine mutex, so work accumulates without limit. Check: count in-flight blocking tasks during the repro.
4. Registry lock (crates/vqtrs-api/src/registry.rs get_or_load) held across a slow load or an eviction (max_loaded = 8) while other requests wait. Check: log lock acquire/release around get_or_load during the repro.

Expected behavior / acceptance
- The server never stops serving: under overload it rejects or queues with a bound (e.g. 429/503 with Retry-After, or 413 for oversized batches), and keeps answering other requests (including a /health endpoint if one exists).
- Add a cap on in-flight embedding work (semaphore) and on batch size (configurable; reject above it instead of attempting it).
- If a wedge can still happen, it must be detectable: a health endpoint that dpty can probe, so dpty restarts the instance instead of reporting Running.

Proof of fix (required)
- A load-test script in the repo (e.g. scripts/ or an ignored integration test) that reproduces triggers 1 and 2 against a locally started vqtrs-api: 8 concurrent clients x 32 texts, and back-to-back 512-text requests, for >= 2 minutes.
- Pass criterion: throughout and after the run, a 1-text probe request answers within 2 s every time; overload produces 429/503/413 responses instead of hangs; RSS stays bounded.
- Show the script failing (wedging) on the current main and passing after the fix.

Context: found while building a Kompressor training dataset (MiniLM retrieval embeddings, ~44k texts). The client side now uses 128-text sequential batches with timeouts and a resumable cache as a workaround. vqtrs is shared by other local tools, which would hang the same way.

Update (same evening): correction, sequential 128-text batches are NOT safe either
- After a fresh restart, 20 consecutive 128-text requests (synthetic and real code chunks) succeeded, but a real dataset build with sequential 128-text batches wedged the server again after ~1,500 texts (around 25 requests in). The client got no response; a 1-text probe timed out (http 000) until `dpty stop --recipe vqtrs/vqtrs-api`.
- So the trigger is not batch size or concurrency alone. Sustained sequential load is enough, which makes hypothesis 1 (memory growth) or 2 (ORT thread pool) more likely than 3 (backlog).
- Reference result for whoever fixes this: the same model (sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, mean pooling, L2-normalized, truncation at 512 tokens) via plain transformers on an RTX 4090 embedded 62,555 texts in 63 s, identical to vqtrs' output (cosine 1.000000 on 11,264 texts). vqtrs on the Mac served ~13-370 texts/s when healthy.
- Note: vqtrs truncates this model at 512 tokens, whereas sentence-transformers' default for all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is 256; any reimplementation or test must use 512 to match existing vectors.
close_reason: Fixed in b938bf6. Root cause: unbounded spawn_blocking inference queued on the engine mutex until tokio's blocking pool (512 threads) saturated - after a burst every request waited forever for a thread while the process sat idle (~0% CPU), matching the reported http 000 / state-U / dpty-still-Running symptoms. Fix: in-flight semaphore acquired as a parts extractor BEFORE the body is read (beyond max_inflight=4 -> 429 + Retry-After + Connection: close, no parse cost, pool can never saturate); max_batch_texts=256 -> 413 (bounds the ONNX arena, which retains the largest batch shape - measured 256x800-char batches retaining ~2.4 GB for a 90 MB model); /health returns 503 + Retry-After while saturated so external probes can detect capacity loss; knobs via config and CLI/env (--max-inflight, --max-batch-texts). Proof per the issue: scripts/loadtest_embeddings.py reproduces triggers 1+2 (+ a retry pile-up burst) for >= 2 min against a locally started server; release-build A/B - main FAIL (0 rejected, no served probe within 15s of the burst, 5/5 after-run probes dead, RSS 2.9 GB unbounded), fixed PASS (234x429 shed, recovery 5.1s, all probes served in 10-20 ms, RSS 2.8 GB bounded by max_inflight x max_batch_texts). Residual, documented: the first probe fired at the exact instant a burst settles can fall in a ~2 s shed window while legitimately admitted batches finish; probes during saturation get 429 in <5 ms and recovery is automatic (main never recovered). Deployed: cargo install --features coreml,qwen3-metal + dpty restart of vqtrs/vqtrs-api on genaihulk; verified live - 300-text batch -> 413, 64-connection burst -> 57x429 + 4x200 with probes still served, /health shows in_flight counts.

title: EmbeddingGemma-2 text embeddings via a candle backend, parity-tested against the Python reference
description:
Add google/embeddinggemma-2 (text path) to vqtrs. fastembed (5.17.3 pinned, 7.1.0 latest) has no support; candle-transformers 0.11.0 ships a Gemma 4 family text tower but returns LM-head logits only, so vqtrs needs its own feature-gated candle backend (same precedent as the qwen3 backend).

- Feature-gated backend (default build unchanged), catalog entry, CLI/API reach it via the normal dense path.
- Text only (vision/audio towers not loaded).

- A Python reference script (transformers / sentence-transformers) dumps embeddings for a fixed text set.
- A parity check compares vqtrs output against the reference: report max abs diff and whether the f32 outputs are bit-identical; same device/dtype (CPU, f32).
- cargo fmt / clippy --workspace --all-targets / test clean.

title: EmbeddingGemma-2 multimodal embeddings (text, image, audio) via a candle backend, parity-tested against the Python reference
description:
Implement google/embeddinggemma-2 via a feature-gated CPU f32 candle backend, including text, images and audio. User expanded the original text-only request to multimodal; video is a separate follow-up vqtrs-1a8h.

Scope delivered:
- Own text, vision and 12-layer conformer audio towers, shared 768-dimensional normalized output space.
- Reference-matched tokenizer/prompts, pixel/JPEG processing, WAV decoding, mel frontend, PyTorch CPU reductions/transcendentals/LayerNorm.
- Catalog plus Engine loading and ordered text/multimodal embedding; CLI feature and embed-media; API feature, text endpoint and inline-base64 /embeddings/multimodal over HTTP/UDS.
- Default ONNX build remains unchanged; all extra dependencies optional. No publishing or production service restart.
- HTTP in-flight and item limits reused; multimodal JSON capped at 16 MiB, no arbitrary remote media fetch/local client path reads. Image dimensions capped at 16,777,216 pixels; CPU sequence cap 8192 including special/media tokens. WAV mono/stereo 16 kHz, clips truncated at 30 sec. Video/other audio formats remain explicit unsupported cases.

Positive-outcome proof:
- Pinned reference checkpoint 914f7f89142e33e77833254d9c9b90c3cef7303b; transformers 5.19.0, torch 2.14.1, sentence-transformers 6.1.0, NumPy 2.4.6, Pillow 12.3.0, macOS Apple Silicon Accelerate, CPU f32, one PyTorch thread. HF text/vision eager, audio SDPA boolean-mask configuration (audio implements its own attention); ST default-SDPA comparison informational only.
- Text 7 cases / 189 tensors, image 7 / 210, audio 5 / 150: 549 tensors, zero differing; max absolute difference zero. Chirp audio module trace also matches all 12 layers and subsampling (43 tensors / zero differing).
- Frontend FFT/magnitude/window/filter/GEMM probes and layernorm goldens match exactly. Audio fixtures include float chirp, short audio, silence, PCM16 speech, 31.5 sec truncation.
- Reproducible scripts and commands in docs/embeddinggemma2-parity.md and justfile. Offline malformed/truncated/non-finite WAV, large-dimension image, token-limit, CLI parser, catalog missing-feature/enabled-feature and HTTP input-schema tests.
- Live disposable server smoke checks mixed text/image/audio HTTP, standard text endpoint, local CLI and warm CLI/UDS vectors byte-for-byte against Python dumps; invalid base64/media, unsupported URLs/paths/models, empty input, item/body limits and health.
- cargo fmt/check, strict workspace all-target Clippy, workspace tests with/without embeddinggemma2.

Bit identity is verified for this pinned platform/reference, not promised for different BLAS/platforms/library versions or arbitrary inputs. Full checkpoint context, GPU backend and video are not claimed.

title: EmbeddingGemma-2 video frame embeddings and container decoding, parity-tested
description:
